title: Rav Chanan bar Moladah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He reports in Rav Huna’s name and is mentioned twice in Sanhedrin 70a. Rashi explains that Moladah is his father’s name. Hyman reports that the old printings have Rabbi Yochanan bar Molada. He traces the error to the Soncino printing, which had Rav Yachnan, and says that the yod dropped from the word Rav, producing “Yochanan.” He cites Dikdukei Soferim.

notes.text: Named Davidson Sanhedrin 70a contains two reports by Rav Chanan of Moladah to Rav Huna, supporting ב״פ as “twice.” Hyman’s Soncino account nevertheless says a yod dropped from רב, an unresolved expression in the supplied notice. That source question remains held; no printed scan or letter-history proof has been obtained.

ב״פ is understood as “twice,” and the supplied folio ע׳ followed by a dot is Sanhedrin 70a. The saved Davidson passage has Rav Chanan bar Moladah reporting in Rav Huna’s name, not speaking to Rav Huna. Hyman reports a Soncino development involving a yod dropping from the word רב; that expression remains unresolved. No Soncino printed page, Dikdukei Soferim apparatus or verified letter history is supplied, and the earlier draft’s treatment of ב״פ as a slip is rejected.

Dikdukei Soferim on Sanhedrin 70a (p. ק, note ר) reports Rabbi Chanan bar Molada for both occurrences in two manuscripts. It reports Rav Yochanan in the first occurrence in the old printings other than Constantinople. It traces that form to Soncino’s Rav Yachnan and reads Rabbi Chanan, as in the nearby Soncino occurrence. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 471) says that the yod dropped from Rav. The apparatus records the forms and its proposed reading; the Soncino page itself has not been independently collated. The consulted Sanhedrin 70a has Chanan reporting in Rav Huna’s name in both passages.
